Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

difficult adjective

hard to do

also hard, tricky, it’s hard to, not easy

classical

Ter. Heaut. 805–806
Catull. 76.13: difficile est longum subitō dēpōnere amōrem
Traupman 304

difficilis, difficile

difficult, hard

“It’s difficult to …” is difficile est with an infinitive; with a verb of saying, the supine: difficile dictū est (Cic. Off. 2.48). Litotes is as common: haud facile, nōn facile.

Other words

  • arduus, ardua, arduum — steep; hard, laborious

    also used · classical · Cic. Or. 33: magnum opus omnīnō et arduum, Brūte, cōnāmur

    First of all “steep”: an uphill task.

Examples

  • Nūlla est tam facilis rēs quīn difficilis siet, quam invītus faciās.

    Nothing is so easy that it isn’t difficult when you do it against your will.Ter. Heaut. 805–806

  • Nihil tam difficile est quīn quaerendō investīgārī possiet.

    Nothing is so difficult that it can’t be tracked down by searching.Ter. Heaut. 675

  • nōn quia difficilia sunt nōn audēmus, sed quia nōn audēmus difficilia sunt

    it is not because things are difficult that we don’t dare; it is because we don’t dare that they are difficultSen. Ep. 104.26

See also difficult, try, easy, hard.

SourcesLewis & Short: difficilis · Lewis & Short: arduus
